topic: agent reliability; benchmark construct validity; distribution shift
status: bounded research-design lead from three lexical-priority full texts and one citation-follow-up; no pooled estimate or novelty claim
claim: An agent benchmark score is conditional on task distribution, action space, horizon, and success metric; high or stable performance on one stratum does not by itself establish reliable performance in a materially different operating regime. Direct evidence here includes task-seed sensitivity within AndroidWorld and sharply different task demands in MobileWorld, but the MobileWorld-versus-AndroidWorld score gap is not a controlled estimate of capability change. EnterpriseArena and the skill-bank audit provide adjacent evidence that long-horizon outcomes and component contributions are also context-dependent, not a common effect size.
positive_evidence: AndroidWorld reports M3A results of 27.6%, 26.3%, and 33.2% across three seeds; in a five-task robustness subset with 20 trials/task, different task parameterizations show greater variance and significant differences for add-expense and edit-note tasks (Sections 5 and Appendix E).

MobileWorld reports a deliberately different workload: 62.2% cross-app workflows and 27.8 average steps versus AndroidWorld's 9.5% and 14.3 under its compared framework; it reports 51.7% for its best agentic framework and 20.9% for its best end-to-end model (Sections 3-4, Tables 6-7).

EnterpriseArena reports 15.4% full-horizon survival across evaluated trials in a 132-month single-company simulator; the authors explicitly limit claims to simulation and an initial single-agent evaluation (Section 4, Appendix J).

The skill-bank audit reports a source-positive skill contribution (+0.084, CI excluding zero) whose target-domain estimate is negative (-0.035) but uncertain (CI includes zero); authors use three seeds and a fixed judge (Section 3.3, Section 5.1).
counterevidence: AndroidWorld is designed for reproducibility and provides state-based reward checks; its 28.4% Pixel 5/Android 12 result is evidence of a useful, controlled alternate-device check, though it does not establish full distribution invariance.

MobileWorld adds different task categories, actions, and longer cross-app workflows, so its lower headline success is expected to reflect task composition and is not an independent same-task failure of AndroidWorld agents.

EnterpriseArena includes ablations that relax environmental constraints and an expert baseline; failures can be diagnosed inside the simulator. However, this does not validate simulator-to-enterprise transfer.
For the skill-transfer example, the HotpotQA point estimate is negative but its confidence interval includes zero; the evidence is directional, not statistically established harm.

sources.sections: Sections 3.3-3.4 and 5; Appendix E.4-E.5; Appendix A
Sections 3-4, especially 4.4-4.6; Tables 6-7; used as out-of-frame citation follow-up, not sample draw

falsifiable_test: Preregister an evaluation of the same frozen agent versions on matched short-horizon tasks, randomized task-parameter variants, long-horizon/cross-app tasks, and tasks requiring user clarification or external tools. Use the same success definition where meaningful, publish stratum-level denominators and confidence intervals, keep step/tool budgets explicit, and independently audit reward verifiers. Compare per-stratum calibration and agent-rank correlations with a predeclared aggregate score. The transportability concern is weakened if rankings and calibrated success estimates remain stable across strata and independent reruns. Not performed in this audit.
limitations: Only three papers are drawn from the lexical-priority arm and one out-of-frame citation follow-up; selection is intentionally not representative. AndroidWorld and MobileWorld workloads/models/actions are not directly matched. EnterpriseArena is a synthetic firm simulator; skill-bank results cover a particular MemSkill framework and fixed judge. No common agents were rerun and no prevalence estimate or causal benchmark-complexity effect was produced.
